This study introduces a novel asynchronous federated learning algorithm designed to address the challenges posed by unbounded gradient norms in resource-constrained mobile devices. While existing literature predominantly assumes bounded gradients, this work demonstrates that such an assumption is unrealistic in practical settings. To handle unbounded updates, the proposed method employs a gradient clipping strategy that dynamically adjusts the clipping threshold based on historical update magnitudes. The algorithm incorporates buffering to accumulate asynchronous updates from participating clients, ensuring efficient processing even when updates arrive at varying times. Theoretical analysis confirms the method's convergence, with the derived bound reflecting the combined effects of unbounded gradients, asynchrony, and buffering. Finally, extensive experiments validate the algorithm's superior performance and efficiency compared to current asynchronous federated learning approaches.

This paper introduces a novel coarse-to-fine, cross-lingual transfer learning framework designed to enhance automatic speech recognition (ASR) performance on low-resource target languages. The approach begins by training a target language ASR system using only coarse-grained, linguistically annotated data. Subsequently, the model leverages the linguistic annotations generated by this initial system to construct a more sophisticated, linguistically annotated corpus. Finally, a refined ASR system is trained on this enhanced dataset. We evaluated the method on the challenging Yoruba language within the Mozilla Common Voice dataset, demonstrating significant performance gains compared to both standard transfer learning techniques and baseline models.

This study introduces a Temporal Difference (TD) learning approach designed to address the navigation challenges of marine robots operating in uncertain environments. To enhance sample efficiency, the method incorporates Gaussian Process (GP) regression within the GP-TD framework, which updates value function estimates using both past and current observations. Furthermore, to manage high-dimensional state spaces, the proposed Sparse GP-TD algorithm employs an inducing point strategy, reducing computational complexity to $O(N)$ per update. The validity of this approach is demonstrated through simulations of a marine robot navigating a complex, unpredictable setting, with results indicating that the Sparse GP-TD method outperforms existing GP-TD variants in terms of both performance and efficiency.

This study examines the relativistic equilibrium of spherical stellar systems characterized by anisotropic, anisotropic two-fluid structures within the framework of General Relativity. We derive the fundamental field equations governing these systems and present a comprehensive analysis of their static, spherically symmetric configurations. By employing the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equation alongside the Einstein field equations, we establish a generalized hydrostatic balance law that incorporates both fluid components and their respective anisotropic stresses. This extended TOV formulation is applied to construct stellar models using various equation of state (EOS) prescriptions. The resulting solutions are analyzed to determine stellar mass, radius, and the profiles of density, pressure, and anisotropy. Furthermore, we investigate the influence of anisotropy on stellar stability and compactness, as well as the impact of the second fluid component on the system's overall characteristics. Finally, we compare our findings with existing literature to validate the results.

Automatic Grammatical Error Correction (GC) has recently advanced through deep learning, yet existing models often struggle with poor generalization when encountering new domains. This challenge is exacerbated in low-resource settings where limited data hampers performance. While few-shot domain adaptation (FS-DA) offers a promising avenue to address this scarcity, current approaches typically fail to account for the inherent diversity found in real-world data. To bridge this gap, we introduce Meta-DA-GEC, a few-shot domain adaptation framework designed for grammatical error correction that leverages meta-learning to handle diverse data sources. Our method trains an initial model using a small set of source domains characterized by varying levels of data diversity. Consequently, the model learns to rapidly adapt to unseen target domains with minimal, diverse-shot examples. We evaluate Meta-DA-GEC on the CoNLL 2012 corpus, demonstrating its effectiveness in adapting to new domains with limited and varied data. Additionally, we assess the framework in cross-task scenarios, showing its ability to transfer knowledge across different GC tasks.

This paper investigates the allocation of indivisible goods among strategic agents with additive valuations, focusing on the trade-off between fairness and efficiency. We examine specific fairness criteria, including envy-freeness up to any item, envy-freeness up to any item for one other agent, proportionality up to any item, and maximin share guarantees. Our analysis establishes that additive valuations allow for the existence of pure Nash equilibria compatible with each of these fairness notions. Furthermore, we provide polynomial-time algorithms to construct allocations that satisfy these fairness conditions alongside a bounded approximation ratio for the social welfare.

We present new optical and near-infrared imaging of the spiral galaxy UGC 8839, revealing a highly distinct, narrow, and luminous central disk surrounded by a classic spiral structure. This inner disk, which we term a "hyper-stable disk," is composed of stars with ages exceeding 1 Gyr and exhibits a scale height approximately 10 times smaller than that of the outer disk. We propose that the extreme stability of this inner region against vertical perturbations results from its high mass-to-light ratio and the presence of a massive dark matter halo. Furthermore, the narrowness of the disk and the galaxy's low specific star formation rate suggest that the outer disk accreted later from the intergalactic medium.

We present a novel method for computing two-current correlations on the lattice, specifically targeting the calculation of the pion's scattering length from vector current correlations. This approach offers a significant advantage over traditional techniques that rely on interpolating operators, as it circumvents the need to determine the pion's mass and decay constant. We demonstrate that this technique is applicable to any two-point correlation function and discuss its broader implications for determining the scattering lengths of other mesons.

We analyzed the optical light curves of XX Cha across multiple bands, utilizing archival data from the TESS mission alongside new observations from the 2.3-meter telescope at the La Silla Observatory. Our findings reveal that XX Cha exhibits highly erratic accretion variability, with the accretion rate fluctuating by a factor of 100 over a span of just 100 days. This extreme behavior is likely driven by the interaction between the circumstellar disk and the stellar magnetosphere, potentially caused by a significant change in the inner disk radius or a dramatic reduction in the accretion shock's radiative efficiency. Furthermore, we demonstrate that such extreme variability can account for the substantial spread in accretion rates typically observed among classical T Tauri stars, even when their global disk properties remain relatively stable.

Offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has recently gained traction, yet existing methods often struggle with poor sample efficiency and fail to leverage the inherent structure of the task. This paper introduces a new offline MARL framework that prioritizes the learning of high-quality trajectories. The proposed approach first identifies the most valuable trajectories within the offline dataset and subsequently employs a generative model to synthesize additional data based on these top trajectories. We validate the method's efficacy through experiments on various multi-agent environments, demonstrating that it outperforms current offline MARL techniques.

This study introduces a novel 2D/3D megavoltage (MV) image registration method based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Addressing the challenge of limited paired 2D/3D training data, we developed a synthetic dataset generator that creates diverse 3D volumes and corresponding 2D projections using a 3D CNN, which were then converted into realistic MV images via Monte Carlo simulation. The proposed CNN architecture was trained on this synthetic data and evaluated against ground truth transformations and a traditional gradient-based optimizer. Results indicate that the model achieves high accuracy, with a mean Dice coefficient of 0.9999 and a mean Hausdorff distance of 0.01 mm. Furthermore, the network offers a significant speed advantage, reducing registration time from approximately 10 minutes to roughly 0.01 seconds.

The concept of quantum nonlocality, first introduced by Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen, has been extensively investigated through various forms of entanglement between distinct particles. Conversely, the potential for nonlocality to manifest between a single-particle state and a local state—termed single-particle entanglement—has remained largely unexplored. This paper demonstrates that such single-particle entanglement indeed generates nonlocal effects, specifically proving the existence of one-sided device-independent nonlocality, or single-particle steering. We establish this by showing that a specific class of one-sided asymmetric states can be uniquely identified using steering, whereas these same states remain indistinguishable under any one-sided device-independent protocol.

The convergence of Blockchain and Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising solution to address the security and privacy challenges inherent in connected cars. This paper presents a systematic review of Blockchain-enabled FL frameworks designed for the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). The authors categorize these frameworks into three distinct groups based on the specific FL algorithms employed: centralized, decentralized, and hybrid approaches. The review examines these frameworks through the lenses of their operational mechanisms, security and privacy protocols, and the specific FL algorithms utilized. Furthermore, the paper outlines the primary contributions of each framework and identifies key open issues and future research directions within this domain.

We present the first comprehensive multi-wavelength observations of V392 Persei, a known dwarf nova that experienced a nova eruption in 2014. Our analysis of these data reveals that V392 Persei is a classic SU UMa-type star, characterized by intermediate outbursts with periods of 30 to 40 days and nuclear outburstances occurring roughly every 100 days. The 2014 nova event was triggered by a thermal instability within the accreted envelope, a phenomenon distinct from the standard nova eruptions typically observed in cataclysmic variables. Furthermore, our findings indicate that V392 Persei is a rare system exhibiting a nova eruption while retaining a white dwarf companion with a mass below 1.1 solar masses.

This paper introduces a novel codebook generation and feedback encoding methodology designed to enhance the accuracy of precoding matrix indicator (PMI) selection in frequency division duplex (FDD) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The proposed approach leverages Gaussian mixture model (GMM) clustering to construct the codebook, offering a more precise representation of the underlying channel distribution compared to conventional techniques. Furthermore, the study details an optimized feedback encoding scheme that incorporates channel quantization bit allocation and codebook subset restriction (CSR) to minimize feedback overhead. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the GMM-based framework, combined with the refined encoding strategy, achieves superior bit-error rate (BER) performance relative to existing methods.

Surface currents, which are robust against disorder and impurities, are a defining characteristic of the quantum Hall effect in three dimensions. While these currents are typically understood to be fragile under nonequilibrium conditions, we demonstrate the existence of robust surface currents in a three-dimensional system of interacting fermions on an optical lattice subjected to a magnetic field. These currents persist even when the system is driven out of equilibrium by a strong, time-periodic force. We attribute this stability to the presence of Floquet-Bloch bands that are topologically nontrivial. Our findings are supported by both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.

This paper establishes a new bound for the rate of Bondi mass loss, demonstrating that it adheres to the inequality $-\dot{M}_{\text{Bondi}} \leqslant \frac{1}{4\pi} \int_{S^2} |\sigma|^2 \mathrm{d}\Omega \leqslant \frac{1}{32\pi} E_{\text{Bondi}}$, where $E_{\text{Bondi}}$ represents the total Bondi energy. This result indicates that the rate of energy radiation cannot surpass one-third of the rate predicted by the News tensor in linearized gravity. Furthermore, we explore the implications of this bound within the context of the Penrose inequality.

We examine the formation and gravitational wave emission of compact object remnants from the initial generation of stars within nuclear star clusters (NSCs) hosting massive young stellar clusters (MYSCs). Our approach involves simulating the dynamical evolution of these systems to determine the masses and trajectories of black holes (BHs) and neutron stars (NSs) at the moment they exit the cluster. We then model the subsequent evolution of these ejected binaries to calculate the rate of mergers within surrounding galaxies. Our findings indicate that BH-BH merger rates can reach up to 100 Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$, a value comparable to rates derived from globular clusters. Furthermore, we demonstrate that BH-NS mergers are a common outcome in these systems, with rates potentially as high as 10 Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$. Finally, we assess the detectability of these events by LIGO/Virgo and future space-based detectors like LISA.

This study introduces a novel multi-carrier wireless system designed for secure communication between a source and a destination, utilizing an amplify-and-forward relay to facilitate data transfer. The system architecture employs orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) at the source and destination, while the relay operates in the frequency domain without OFDM capabilities. A specific subcarrier pairing strategy is developed to optimize the secure transmission rate, ensuring that the source and destination transmit exclusively on paired subcarriers. The resulting secure rate optimization problem is formulated as a non-convex task, which is addressed through an iterative algorithm. This approach involves iteratively selecting the most suitable subcarrier pairings to maximize secure throughput, followed by determining the optimal power allocation for the selected pairs. Numerical simulations validate the proposed method, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing secure data transmission rates.

Text-based games serve as an excellent platform for training language models and testing artificial intelligence. However, current simulation tools often fall short in performance, typically executing only a few hundred game steps per second. This low throughput creates a major bottleneck when running large-scale simulations, which are necessary to generate the vast amounts of data required for effective model scaling. To address this, we introduce TextWorldExpress, a high-performance engine capable of running at over one million steps per second. By leveraging C++ and several key optimizations, TextWorldExpress achieves a speedup of more than 3,000 times compared to existing solutions. This dramatic increase in speed allows for the generation of petabytes of synthetic text data, enabling us to train a new model named TextPaLM-2. Testing reveals that TextPaLM-2 outperforms its predecessors in both natural language understanding and role-playing tasks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that simulating games at such extreme velocities can facilitate the training of larger-scale language models.

This study introduces a hardware and algorithm co-design framework for processing video data using Hierarchical Tucker Tensor (HTT) Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The proposed approach leverages a hierarchical Tucker tensor decomposition of the weight matrices to optimize both computational efficiency and memory usage. To further enhance performance, the design incorporates a specialized hardware architecture featuring a dedicated Tucker engine alongside a hierarchical memory hierarchy. Additionally, the system employs a dynamic scheduling strategy that prioritizes the most critical tensor cores to maximize throughput. Experimental results demonstrate that this solution achieves a 1.5x increase in throughput and a 1.5x reduction in energy consumption compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

We introduce a conjecture within the context of Conformal Field Theory (CFT) that serves as a counterpart to the Weak Gravity Conjecture (WGC). This proposal, termed the Charged Operator Conjecture (COC), posits that in any unitary, irrational, two-dimensional ($d=2$) CFT, there must exist a primary operator $\mathcal{O}$ with conformal dimension $\Delta$ and $U(1)$ charge $q$ such that the ratio $q^2/\Delta$ exceeds a specific constant. We demonstrate that this conjecture is consistent with the existence of a well-defined, convex region in the $(q^2/\Delta)$ parameter space. Furthermore, we provide evidence supporting the COC through the analysis of specific, exactly solvable models, including the $U(1)_k$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model and the $U(1)_k$ compactified free boson.

This paper demonstrates that within an excellent local ring containing a field, the tightness of the Hilbert polynomial for all parameter ideals serves as a necessary and sufficient condition for the ring to be $F$-regular. Furthermore, in the context of a complete local ring with residue field characteristic $p > 0$, the $F$-rationality of the ring is equivalent to the tightness of the Hilbert polynomial for every parameter ideal.

This paper introduces a novel ancillary services acquisition model designed to support the procurement of frequency regulation and voltage control services. The model operates under a hierarchical framework where the upper level functions as a mixed-integer linear program to determine optimal procurement quantities and supplier selections, while the lower level simulates market clearing to establish prices based on supply and demand dynamics. By integrating these layers, the approach captures the feedback loop between procurement decisions and resulting market prices. The study details the model's formulation, solution methodology, and validation through numerical experiments. These simulations demonstrate that accounting for market interactions yields more accurate procurement strategies and superior outcomes for both the system operator and market participants.

This work examines the $n$-th iterate of a polynomial $f$ over a field $K$, denoted as $f^{\circ n}$, and investigates the conditions under which this iterate can be expressed as a specialization of a polynomial $g$ with coefficients in $K[x]$, such that $g(x, f)^{\circ n} = f^{\circ n}$. We establish that if $f$ is not a polynomial in $h^{\circ k}$ for some $k$ dividing $n$, then such a $g$ exists if and only if $f$ is a prime element within the ring $K[x][y]$. Furthermore, we determine the precise conditions for $f$ to be prime in $K[x][y]$ when $K$ is either the field of rational or algebraic integers.

Saturn's stratospheric polar vortex, which typically forms during the winter and reaches its peak in the spring, usually dissipates by mid-summer. However, this year, the 2020-2021 polar vortex has persisted into the summer, exhibiting a hexagonal shape similar to the famous polar hexagon observed in the planet's troposphere. This phenomenon is notable because the stratospheric vortex is expected to collapse under the influence of planetary waves and the Coriolis effect once the sun rises above the horizon. Utilizing data from the Cassini spacecraft, we demonstrate that the current Saturnian polar hexagon is a transient feature, likely resulting from the interaction between the polar vortex and planetary waves.

This work examines the Cauchy problem for nonlinear Schrödinger equations with an obstacle in the exterior domain $\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\Omega$, where $\Omega$ represents a bounded region with a smooth boundary. We establish that if the initial data $u_0$ lies in the energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\Omega)$ and possesses sufficiently high energy and low mass relative to a ground state soliton, the corresponding solution will blow up in finite time. Furthermore, we demonstrate that any such blow-up solution must converge, up to spatial translations, to a sum of the obstacle and a soliton as time approaches its maximal existence interval.

This paper examines semi-parametric local uniform reductions for varieties defined over the integral closure within the field of rational functions of a finitely generated $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra $A$, where that algebra contains at least one positive characteristic $p$. We establish that if a variety $X$ over such an $A$ admits a global uniform reduction, then it necessarily possesses a local uniform reduction characterized by a constant $C$ that remains independent of the characteristic $p$. Conversely, we demonstrate that the implication does not hold in reverse: the existence of a global uniform reduction cannot be deduced solely from the presence of a local uniform reduction.

This paper introduces the concept of the linearisation of a graded bundle, which is defined as a specific type of polarization within the associated graded category. We examine the fundamental properties of these linearisations and demonstrate that any symplectic or Poisson structure on a graded bundle naturally induces a corresponding symplectic or Poisson structure on its linearisation. Furthermore, we explore the relationship between the various geometric structures defined on graded bundles and those on their linearisations.

This paper examines the normalization of Haar measures on $GL_n$ and its associated unipotent subgroups within a $p$-adic field $\mathbb{F}$, with the specific objective of determining the integral of the characteristic function of the unipotent variety. The findings indicate that this integral equals $q^{n^2/2}(1+O(q^{-1}))$, where $q$ denotes the cardinality of the residue field of $\mathbb{F}$.

The recovery of a field's phase from its measured intensity, known as phase retrieval, is a vital technique across numerous disciplines. While traditionally applied to imaging, this method has recently been adapted for spectroscopy, particularly in the X-ray domain. However, existing approaches face constraints regarding the number of required scans and often lack the ability to reconstruct the phase of individual spectral components. This study introduces a novel nuclear phase retrieval spectroscopy method utilizing X-ray scattering at the K-edge. By leveraging the intrinsic atomic nature of X-ray absorption edges, the approach successfully reconstructs the complete complex reflectivity spectrum from just two scans. Furthermore, the reconstructed data reveals the phase of individual spectral features, offering new insights into the dynamics of atomic motion during photo-induced nuclear dissociation.

This study introduces a hybridized mixed finite element method designed to model single-phase Darcy flow within fractured porous media. The approach treats the domain as a combination of a bulk material and a network of fractures, where the latter are represented by interfaces possessing distinct permeability characteristics. The resulting discrete system is derived from a mixed formulation of the Darcy equation, incorporating a hybridized version of the continuity constraint. This constraint is enforced exclusively on the internal boundaries separating the bulk and fractures, while the bulk faces internal boundaries are relaxed. The method's validity is demonstrated through numerical experiments that examine the influence of varying fracture permeability on flow behavior.

This paper introduces a suite of R-based workflows designed to facilitate the application of Bayes Factors for model comparison. These tools support the entire analytical lifecycle, from data preparation and model specification to the visualization of results. The authors illustrate the practical implementation of these workflows through a case study involving the comparison of linear and nonlinear models fitted to a dataset of US presidential approval ratings.

Discourse markers, such as *well*, *you know*, and *actually*, are frequently employed in spoken language to regulate the flow of conversation and express the speaker's attitude. Despite their significance, these words are often excluded from standard linguistic resources like WordNet and are typically omitted from semantic role labeling tasks. This study introduces a novel approach to the automatic semantic annotation of discourse markers. We present a new dataset comprising 1,000 manually labeled instances of discourse markers extracted from the WikiText-2 corpus. Furthermore, we propose a new taxonomy for discourse marker semantics and develop an automated system to assign semantic roles to these markers within text. We evaluate this system using both human judges and a baseline model, demonstrating its efficacy through strong agreement with expert annotators.

Matrix factorization stands as a cornerstone technique in matrix completion, collaborative filtering, and numerous other matrix recovery tasks. This study introduces a unified global landscape analysis for fixed-rank matrix optimization, employing Riemannian geometry to address both convex and nonconvex scenarios. By treating the fixed-rank constraint as a submanifold within the ambient Euclidean space, the authors demonstrate that, under mild conditions, the objective function becomes geodesically convex when factorized into a specific rank. This finding implies that local minimization methods are guaranteed to converge to a global minimum. Furthermore, the analysis extends to general nonconvex objectives, proving that the factorized objective exhibits geodesic convexity on a local neighborhood around the global optimum. Consequently, any local minimum within this vicinity qualifies as a global solution. These insights offer a streamlined, geometrically intuitive framework applicable to a wide array of matrix optimization challenges.

A strong edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is defined as an edge-coloring where no two edges sharing a common endpoint or a common neighbor share the same color. This paper establishes the existence of a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph with chromatic number 5 for its strong edges, thereby determining the strong edge-chromatic number of such graphs to be exactly 5.

This study introduces a coevolutionary genetic algorithm designed to generate Nash equilibria within a symmetric Cournot framework featuring a nonlinear inverse demand curve. In this proposed algorithm, each individual in the population represents a distinct strategy, defined by a specific output level. Interactions between individuals are simulated through a game where payoffs are determined by the outputs of both participants. Selection for the next generation occurs based on these payoffs, with offspring created via crossover and mutation operators. The primary innovation lies in the fitness evaluation method: an individual's fitness is calculated as the average payoff it yields against every other member of the population. The results indicate that this algorithm successfully generates a Nash equilibrium for the specified game.

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a weighted oriented graph, and let $I(\mathcal{D})$ represent its edge ideal within the polynomial ring $R$ associated with the variables of $\mathcal{D}$. This paper establishes that for any vertex cover $\mathcal{C}$ of $\mathcal{D}$, the ordinary powers of $I(\mathcal{D})$ are contained within the symbolic powers corresponding to $\mathcal{C}$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that if $\mathcal{D}$ possesses a Hamiltonian path, then the symbolic powers of $I(\mathcal{D})$ coincide with its ordinary powers.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in computer vision tasks, yet their vulnerability to adversarial attacks remains a significant concern. While existing research has explored various defenses, this paper introduces a novel approach utilizing activation range supervision to enhance robustness against adversarial examples. We demonstrate that this method effectively mitigates attacks by constraining the output magnitudes of neurons within the network. Furthermore, we establish a formal safety case that substantiates the robustness guarantees provided by this technique.

This work examines the Jordanian twists generated by a specific class of $1$-parameter Lie algebra deformations. We demonstrate that these twists generate a novel family of non-conformal $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded quantum torus algebras. Furthermore, we establish the existence of a unique irreducible highest weight representation for these algebras and derive their explicit structure.

Building a multilingual common semantic space is crucial for cross-lingual natural language processing, yet it remains a significant challenge due to the vast linguistic diversity across languages. This study introduces a novel cluster-consistent word embedding approach designed to establish such a shared semantic space. The core premise is that words sharing similar meanings should exhibit consistent clustering patterns across different languages. To validate this, we propose a new clustering-based objective function that enforces cluster consistency between multilingual word embeddings. Our method operates in two stages: first, it generates initial embeddings for each language independently using standard techniques; second, it aligns these embeddings by optimizing the proposed objective function. We evaluated our approach on two distinct tasks: multilingual word similarity assessment and cross-lingual text classification. The results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art baselines.

This study presents new measurements of inclusive charged pion, kaon, (anti-)proton, and $\phi$ meson production in Xe-Xe collisions at the CERN Large Hadron Collider, conducted at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.44$ TeV. Data were collected using the ALICE experiment with an integrated luminosity of $620\,\mu\text{b}^{-1}$. For each identified particle species, yields are reported as a function of transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) across various centrality classes, defined by the fraction of the nucleon-nucleon collision, $0.05 < \text{V}_{\rm ch} < 0.95$. Additionally, particle ratios relative to charged pions are provided as functions of $p_{\rm T}$ and centrality. These results are compared against predictions from several theoretical models, including EPOS LHC, DPM ZH2, HIING, and AMPT.

In the aftermath of the Chilean riots of October 2019, which resulted in over 1,000 fatalities and widespread destruction, this study presents a novel non-local epidemiological model designed to simulate the unrest. This approach diverges from conventional local models by incorporating a non-local term that accounts for the influence of unrest in surrounding areas on specific neighborhoods. The non-local component is defined through a convolution integral, utilizing a kernel function to represent the impact of unrest in other regions on a given location. The paper details the mathematical formulation, including the derivation of a unique solution and its stability, and offers a numerical method for solving the system. Furthermore, the authors apply the model to the Chilean context, calibrating it with actual data to generate simulations that align with historical events. The findings indicate that the non-local model provides a more accurate representation of the riots than local alternatives, effectively capturing the spatial propagation of violence. Ultimately, this research offers a sophisticated tool for analyzing civil disturbances, with potential applications in urban planning and public policy formulation.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm for determining the solvability of inclusion and subsethood constraints between extended regular expressions (ERE), which support character classes, the Kleene star, and the union operator. The proposed method relies on a specific class of regular expressions termed symbolic deterministic finite automata (S-DFA). These S-DFA structures utilize symbolic transitions to represent extended character classes and employ deterministic branching to model the Kleene star. The resulting algorithm operates in time complexity exponential relative to the size of the input EREs but remains linear with respect to the length of their strings.

Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) is a critical technology for estimating the pose of robots operating in GPS-denied environments. While deep learning-based VIO methods have recently emerged as promising alternatives to traditional hand-crafted algorithms, they currently face significant challenges regarding the high computational costs of processing raw sensor data and the lack of effective mechanisms to utilize historical information for improving real-time performance. To address these issues, we introduce EMA-VIO, a novel visual-inertometric odometry framework that employs external memory attention (EMA) to process point clouds. This approach streamlines point cloud data by filtering outliers and down-sampling points, while the EMA mechanism dynamically adjusts the importance of each point based on its historical relevance and current significance. Our framework integrates a deep learning-based VIO pipeline with an end-to-end trainable system that utilizes a PointNet-based encoder to extract features from processed point clouds, a bidirectional LSTM to model temporal dependencies, and a decoder to predict pose changes and optimize initial values for pose graph optimization. Extensive evaluations on both real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate that EMA-VIO achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in terms of trajectory error and computational efficiency.

This study examines a data completion problem for time-harmonic Maxwell equations within a bounded domain, where the objective is to determine the missing permittivity in a sub-region based on known electric field measurements inside that region. The analysis relies on a quasi-reversibility approach, utilizing a specific regularization technique to ensure the well-posedness of the associated variational problem. Furthermore, the research establishes the existence of an approximate solution that converges to the true solution as measurement noise diminishes. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the method's efficacy.

Federated knowledge graphs (KGs) represent a growing trend in knowledge representation, where multiple parties collaboratively amalgamate knowledge graphs without disclosing their underlying data sources. A significant hurdle in federated KG construction is the lack of a unified schema, which results in diverse graph structures and varying semantic representations of entities and relations. To address this, we introduce Federated Selective Aggregation (FedSelect), a framework designed to integrate these distributed graphs into a cohesive, high-quality knowledge base. FedSelect operates in two primary stages: first, it identifies and incorporates only the most pertinent knowledge triples, filtering out noise and irrelevant data; second, it resolves structural and semantic conflicts among the selected triples. We propose a novel conflict resolution mechanism that leverages a probabilistic semantic similarity metric to determine the optimal triples for retention. We validate FedSelect through extensive experiments on both real-world datasets and a simulated scenario, demonstrating its efficacy in creating robust federated knowledge graphs.

This paper investigates the rank growth of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ within $D$ and $D'$ quartic extensions, where $D$ and $D'$ are the two non-isomorphic quartic fields sharing the same quadratic subfield and discriminant, with Galois groups $S_4$ and $A_4$, respectively. We establish that the average growth in rank across these $S_4$ and $A_4$ extensions is identical. Furthermore, we derive an explicit formula for this average growth in terms of the $2$-Selmer ranks of the curves over the quadratic subfield and the two cubic subfields of the $D$ extension.

We examine the evolution of entanglement entropy in two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) with two spatial dimensions following a holographic quench, where the pre-quench state is a vacuum perturbed by a local operator. By applying the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) alongside the principle of entanglement monotonicity, we establish rigorous upper limits on the rate at which entanglement grows. These bounds are found to be saturated by the quenched states generated by the specific operator dimensions relevant to our analysis. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these same bounds are saturated by the dual gravitational description of the quench, where the process is modeled as a shockwave propagating through anti-de Sitter space. Finally, we extend this framework to scenarios involving multiple quenches, deriving new constraints on the mutual information growth rate.

This study introduces a class of coherence measures defined by the asymmetry of a state's probability distribution across measurement outcomes. These measures are shown to function as robust tools for quantifying the distinguishability between quantum states. Furthermore, they are employed to derive tight, coherence-asymmetry-based bounds on the rates of unitary evolution. The research also investigates the relationship between these newly defined measures and established coherence metrics, specifically examining their connection to the asymmetry monotone-based bounds on quantum speed limits.

This paper examines the interpolation projector $P_n$ associated with a set of nodes $\{x_k\}_{k=0}^n$ within the space $C[-1,1]$. We establish a new estimate for the uniform norm of this projector, expressed as $\|P_n\| \leq \exp\left(\sup_{x \in [-1,1]} V_n(x)\right) + 1$, where $V_n(x)$ denotes the discrete Chebyshev-Wronskian function. Furthermore, we analyze the specific case where nodes are the roots of the classical Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.

Superconducting quantum circuits are increasingly dependent on the development of advanced packaging and fabrication techniques, which often introduce defects that degrade performance. To address this, near-field terahertz nanoscopy is emerging as a powerful tool for identifying such imperfections. This paper demonstrates the application of near-field terahertz nanoscopy to investigate coplanar microwave resonators, revealing that the near-field distribution of their resonant modes extends significantly beyond the physical boundaries of the structures. The study further explores the impact of various geometric parameters on these near-field characteristics and presents a theoretical model that accurately predicts the observed spatial profiles. Finally, the authors suggest that this enhanced understanding of near-field behavior will facilitate the optimization of superconducting quantum devices.

This paper examines the long-term atmospheric evolution of Venus, with a specific focus on the mechanisms driving the loss of its primordial hydrogen-rich atmosphere and the subsequent rise in surface temperatures to approximately 735 K. We analyze the role of hydrodynamic escape, the photochemical processing of organic molecules, and the degassing of volatiles from the planetary surface. Furthermore, we explore the positive feedback loop between surface warming and the enhanced solubility of CO2 in surface oceans, which may have triggered a runaway greenhouse effect. Finally, we address the negative feedback mechanisms, such as the photochemical destruction of methane and the sequestration of CO2 into surface carbonates, that likely contributed to the current atmospheric composition.

Multivariate point process models are frequently utilized to analyze and forecast events within fields such as finance, telecommunications, and neuroscience. Among these, the multivariate self-exciting Hawkes process is a prominent choice, particularly for its ability to model mutual influences between different event types. However, estimating the parameters of multivariate Hawkes processes remains challenging due to the non-identifiability of these parameters and the inherent difficulty in obtaining maximum likelihood estimates. This study introduces a Bayesian approach for parameter estimation in multivariate Hawkes processes that incorporates non-linearities. We evaluate the proposed method through both simulation experiments and real-world data analysis, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling complex event dynamics.

High-intensity laser pulses interacting with magnetized plasmas can experience simultaneous polarization transformation and amplification, a phenomenon driven by the distinct nonlinear refractive indices experienced by left- and right-circularly polarized light. This effect enables the generation of multi-petawatt laser pulses with altered polarization states. We present a theoretical framework that accurately models this process, accounting for both the nonlinear refractive index and the ponderomotive force. Our analysis demonstrates that, under specific conditions, this mechanism can yield polarization conversion accompanied by a 100% increase in intensity. Furthermore, we identify the optimal parameters required to achieve this simultaneous amplification and transformation.

We present a new analysis of the tau lepton electric dipole moment (EDM) search utilizing data collected at the Belle II detector. This study focuses on the decay mode $e^{\pm}\gamma$, where the signal is identified by reconstructing the remaining particles from the decay of the parent $\tau^{\mp}$ lepton. The analysis incorporates a refined background estimation technique based on a data-driven approach and employs a maximum likelihood method to determine the significance of any potential signal. The results indicate no observable signal, leading to an updated constraint on the complex form factor $|f_{EDM}|$ at the 90\% confidence level: $|f_{EDM}| < 1.1 \times 10^{-4} \text{ GeV}^{-1}$. This finding corresponds to a 90\% confidence limit of $d_{\tau} < 1.1 \times 10^{-17} \text{ e cm}$ for the tau lepton EDM.

This work examines the decoding of rank metric codes under the assumption that an error matrix possesses a low symmetric rank. We establish that if an error matrix $E$ has a symmetric rank $d$ and the code's minimum rank distance is $2d+1$, then any such error can be uniquely identified and corrected. Furthermore, we present an algorithm with a time complexity of $O(n^3)$ capable of decoding any error matrix with a symmetric rank $d$ for a code with minimum rank distance $2d+2$.

Recently, a new OPE block was introduced that streamlines the computation of four-point correlation functions in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ by serving as a building block for four-point functions involving two external primary fields with spins $s_1$ and $s_2$. This new construction was shown to be a special instance of an infinite sum of twist operators, a concept previously explored in the context of AdS/CFT. In this paper, we examine this spinning OPE block from the perspective of the AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ duality. We demonstrate that the block can be expressed as a path integral over AdS$_3$ space, where the integrand consists of a Witten diagram featuring two bulk-to-boundary propagators and two bulk-to-bulk propagators connecting the respective internal line to the external legs. Furthermore, we establish a direct correspondence between this spinning OPE block and the spinning conformal block within the two-dimensional CFT.

This note offers a new proof of the combinatorial formula for Pontrjagin classes originally established by Gelfand and MacPherson in their 1973 paper. The derivation relies on the cobordism relation and the splitting principle, utilizing the specific properties of Pontrjagin classes within the cohomology ring of complex projective space.

We present new optical and near-infrared spectroscopic data alongside new optical photometry for SN 2020jfo, a Type II supernova characterized by a short plateau. This object was observed repeatedly using the 2.3-m Isaac Newton Telescope at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory in the Canary Islands. Our analysis indicates that SN 2020jfo is a hydrogen-rich explosion of a massive star, featuring a photospheric temperature of approximately 6000 K during the plateau phase and a mass of roughly 10 solar masses of 56Ni synthesized. The spectral characteristics during the plateau phase align with those of other Type II-P supernovae, yet the early spectra display prominent features of high-velocity, hydrogen-poor ejecta. This paper introduces a novel design for Multiplexed Lobster-Eye Optics (MLO) aimed at enhancing the field of view (FoV) of X-ray telescopes. This concept integrates Lobster-Eye Optics (LEO) with a multiplexing scheme previously developed for grazing-incidence Wolter telescopes. The proposed MLO architecture consists of a two-layer arrangement: the first layer features a 3D-printed LEO structure, while the second layer comprises a 2D grid of 3D-printed LEO elements oriented at 90 degrees relative to the first. This configuration enables the system to capture a significantly larger FoV compared to traditional LEO designs. The paper details the design methodology, presents simulation outcomes, and provides a physical prototype demonstrating the feasibility of the concept.

This work introduces a novel concept termed "level set uniform ellipticity," which generalizes the standard definition of uniform ellipticity. We establish that this new condition is equivalent to a specific form of "partial uniform ellipticity" recently defined by the authors. Furthermore, we examine the level set version of the divergence structure and analyze the regularity properties of solutions within this framework.

The dark matter halo mass function (HMF) serves as a fundamental probe of cosmological models, yet accurately predicting it remains a significant challenge. This study introduces a novel methodology to forecast the HMF by integrating deep neural networks with velocity field analysis. We trained a neural network using dark matter halo data from $N$-body simulations across a broad spectrum of cosmological parameters, including $\Omega_{\rm m}$, $\sigma_8$, and $\Lambda$CDM variations. The model successfully learned the intricate dependencies between halo properties and these cosmological drivers, enabling it to predict the HMF with high precision. Crucially, we discovered that incorporating the velocity field of dark matter halos allows for a more accurate HMF prediction than relying on mass alone. Specifically, the velocity-to-dispersion ratio ($V_{\rm max}/\sigma$) emerged as a highly effective parameter for characterizing dark matter halos. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the velocity-to-dispersion ratio is intrinsically linked to halo formation history and the underlying cosmological parameters. These findings suggest that the velocity field provides essential insights into dark matter halo evolution, offering a promising avenue for future research into their formation and development.

This work introduces a new numerical framework designed to simulate the rotational evolution of compact stars under the influence of magnetic fields and magnetic braking. The methodology relies on a novel, fully relativistic treatment of hydrostatic equilibrium in rotating systems, which incorporates a new formulation for the angular momentum evolution equation. This equation is derived from the conservation of the stress-energy tensor and the conservation of magnetic flux, both within the presence of magnetic fields and magnetic braking. The approach is validated by comparing results against existing literature for various test cases, including the evolution of magnetic flux, magnetic braking, and the development of differential rotation. Furthermore, the code is applied to investigate the long-term rotational evolution of neutron stars, specifically examining the impact of magnetic braking and magnetic fields on spin-down behavior and the generation of differential rotation.

Accurately extracting information from complex, visually dense documents is a critical capability for many enterprise applications. While deep learning models have demonstrated significant promise in this domain, their widespread adoption is hindered by the substantial expenses associated with collecting and labeling extensive training datasets. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel, cost-effective data-labeling methodology that leverages a lightweight, pre-trained model to automatically generate high-quality, pseudo-labeled datasets. Our approach utilizes a two-stage process: first, a lightweight model trained on a small, manually curated dataset predicts the bounding boxes for key-value pairs; second, these predictions are used to create a pseudo-dataset for training a more sophisticated, end-to-end extraction model. We evaluated this framework using a real-world dataset of invoices, demonstrating that the end-to-end model trained on our pseudo-data achieved performance comparable to a model trained on the original, fully labeled dataset, but required only a fraction of the initial labeling effort.

Gravitational wave (GW) observations of neutron star-black hole (NSBH) mergers are anticipated to provide significant insights into compact object astrophysics, including the formation and evolution of binary systems, the origins of short gamma-ray bursts, and the synthesis of heavy elements via the rapid neutron-capture process (r-process). However, distinguishing NSBH mergers from black hole-black hole (BHBH) mergers remains a major challenge due to the scarcity of GW events and the difficulty in identifying the presence of a neutron star. This study employs deep learning techniques to detect and classify NSBH mergers using simulated GW signals generated by numerical relativity. We introduce a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture designed to classify NSBH events against BHBH events, achieving a 99.99\% accuracy rate for detection and a 99.98\% accuracy rate for classification. Furthermore, we developed a new CNN architecture specifically for estimating NSBH merger parameters, which demonstrated a 10\% improvement in parameter estimation accuracy compared to existing methods. Finally, we applied these models to real data from the second observing run of Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo (O2), successfully identifying 11 NSBH candidates from the GWOpen O2 catalog.

Urban interactions are vital for fostering innovation and economic growth, yet the pandemic-induced shift toward remote activities has significantly altered their frequency and variety. This study investigates how these behavioral shifts impacted the diversity of urban encounters across 100 U.S. cities. By analyzing mobile phone data from 2019 and 2020, we observed that while the overall volume of urban interactions declined by 20% in 2020, the diversity of these encounters dropped even more sharply, by 30%. This reduction was driven primarily by decreased visits to less common destination types, such as workplaces, which are typically crucial for generating new ideas. Furthermore, the impact varied geographically: cities with initially higher income diversity saw a steeper decline in the variety of urban interactions. Ultimately, the research indicates that pandemic-related behavioral changes have likely contributed to a diminished capacity for innovation and economic expansion.

We present a new hydrodynamic simulation framework designed to model the episodic accretion and growth of massive protostars, with a specific focus on the impact of stellar outflows and supernova explosions. Our results indicate that outflows and supernovae are critical for regulating the accretion process, preventing the formation of stars significantly more massive than the initial target. We also find that the process of assembling stellar mass is episodic, characterized by distinct phases of rapid accretion separated by intervals of reduced accretion rates. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the merger of protostars is a common occurrence during this growth phase, with the likelihood of such mergers increasing as the total stellar mass increases.

This work examines the evolution of water surface elevation in the presence of constant vorticity, extending the analysis beyond the standard assumption of zero background vorticity. By applying a canonical transformation, the system is reformulated as a set of coupled nonlinear ordinary differential equations, which are subsequently expressed within a Hamiltonian framework. This approach facilitates the derivation of a Dysthe-type equation incorporating constant vorticity, achieved through a specific canonical transformation of the Hamiltonian that eliminates all terms up to third order in the small parameter $\epsilon$. The resulting equation, identified as a Hamiltonian Dysthe equation with constant vorticity, is shown to be equivalent to the original initial value problem up to an order of $\epsilon^4$. Furthermore, the paper investigates the conservation of this new equation and provides a detailed comparison between its solutions and those of the classical Dysthe equation.

This paper introduces the definition of differential forms and the Stokes formula within the context of locally convex spaces equipped with a specific type of measure. It further establishes the existence of forms possessing non-vanishing integrals over spheres, utilizing the Stokes formula as a key tool.

This paper introduces a real-time navigation framework for an unmanned surface vehicle (USV) that integrates a dynamic Bayesian filter to fuse data from a GPS and a 2D sonar. Designed to operate in coastal environments, the system leverages the sonar's ability to detect underwater obstacles and map the water surface, while the GPS provides precise position tracking. The proposed controller employs a virtual structure approach, utilizing the dynamic Bayesian filter to generate a real-time, high-resolution map of the water surface. This allows the USV to navigate safely by avoiding submerged and surface obstacles while adhering to predefined trajectories. The study details the implementation of the virtual structure controller, the specific fusion algorithm, and the resulting real-time navigation capabilities.

The rapid proliferation of social media has significantly altered how information is disseminated, creating a fertile ground for misinformation and fake news that can cause substantial harm. This study introduces a novel approach to fake news detection by leveraging automatic text summarization. The proposed method trains a neural abstractive summarization model to generate summaries of news articles, which are then used as features for a classifier to identify fake news. Experiments conducted on the Twitter Fake News dataset demonstrate that this method achieves a 99.99% accuracy rate.

This study examines the curvature effect within Gaussian random fields, a phenomenon where the field's variance increases as the domain's curvature rises. We establish a precise mathematical relationship linking this curvature effect to the field's covariance function. Furthermore, we analyze specific instances of Gaussian random fields, including the Matérn process, to illustrate how the curvature effect varies across different scenarios.

This study introduces a proximal gradient algorithm designed for rotationally invariant weighted $\ell_1$-norm principal component analysis (PCA). We establish that the proposed algorithm achieves linear convergence to a stationary point, provided the weighting function adheres to specific mild conditions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the algorithm attains linear convergence to a global minimizer when the weighting function exhibits power-law behavior. These findings represent the first demonstration of linear convergence to a global minimum for non-convex $\ell_1$-norm PCA under general rotation-invariant weighting schemes. Finally, we present extensive numerical experiments validating the algorithm's efficacy and efficiency.

This study introduces HiTMap, a novel hierarchical topological map designed for navigation in unfamiliar settings. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on global Euclidean representations, HiTMap utilizes a structured hierarchy of nodes and edges to depict the environment. This method offers distinct advantages, including reduced memory consumption, faster computational processing, and enhanced robustness against errors. Furthermore, the modular nature of the map facilitates the integration of diverse navigation algorithms. To validate the system, we conducted extensive evaluations in both simulated and real-world scenarios, demonstrating HiTMap's superior performance in efficiency, robustness, and overall navigational capability compared to existing methods.

Atomic interferometry is emerging as a highly sensitive technique for measuring local magnetic fields, offering significant potential for characterizing magnetic anomalies in geology, archaeology, and security applications. This study introduces a novel method that combines atomic interferometry with a superconducting plate to detect magnetic field variations caused by the Meissner effect. We demonstrate that this approach enables the sensitive identification of local magnetic field changes through the modulation of the atomic interferometer's phase shift. Furthermore, we show that the sensitivity of this method can be significantly enhanced by increasing the atomic momentum. Ultimately, this work establishes a new pathway for the precise, sensitive detection of local magnetic field changes driven by the Meissner effect.

This work introduces a novel framework for finite admixture models, which are defined as stochastic geometric structures on a finite Choquet simplex. These models are designed to generate a distribution over finite admixtures, where an admixture consists of a probability vector paired with a set of samples drawn from those probabilities. We establish the existence and uniqueness of these models and derive their explicit construction for specific cases. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed structures are equivalent to previously defined models, including the Dirichlet-multinomial and the Mallows mixture.

DynaSOAr is a novel parallel memory allocator designed for GPU object-oriented programming, addressing the scarcity of existing allocators for GPU OOP environments. This allocator integrates a dynamic, coarse-grained, and coarse-grained memory management strategy with a parallel memory access mechanism. It operates by first partitioning the total memory into fixed-size blocks, which are then allocated in parallel to multiple objects. To ensure efficient utilization, DynaSOAr employs a dynamic algorithm to determine the optimal allocation size for each object. Furthermore, it implements a parallel memory access algorithm that allows multiple threads to retrieve objects simultaneously. The allocator's efficiency and effectiveness were validated through extensive benchmarking and comparative analysis against established memory allocators.

This study presents a relativistic first-principles investigation into the magnetic states of an Mn adatom and Mn dimers situated on a Nb(110) surface. The research focuses on the determination of the $s$-wave component within the in-gap Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) states, which are induced by these magnetic impurities. The $s$-wave character is extracted from the projected spin-resolved density of states (PSR-DOS) along the $k$-axis perpendicular to the surface, utilizing a method that circumvents the need for explicit wavefunction retrieval. The findings indicate that the YSR states associated with both the adatom and dimers possess a significant $s$-wave contribution. Furthermore, the research reveals that the magnetic moment of the Mn adatom diminishes upon adsorption, while the moment of the Mn dimer remains largely unaffected. Finally, the study demonstrates that the in-gap states for both configurations exhibit a strong dependence on the magnetic moment of the constituent Mn atoms.

Located 100 pc away, the newly identified TOI-712 system consists of three mini-Neptune planets orbiting an M3.5V star with a mass of 0.57 solar masses. The planets, designated TOI-712 b, c, and d, have radii ranging from 2.3 to 3.1 Earth radii and orbital periods between 4.5 and 14.5 days. We present the discovery of the outermost planet, TOI-712 d, which was initially identified via TESS photometry and subsequently confirmed through high-precision radial velocity measurements obtained with the HARPS and CARMENES spectrographs. Our analysis of the system's architecture reveals a distinct lack of orbital circularization and compositional evolution among the planets, characteristics typical of an adolescent planetary system. Furthermore, the innermost planet, TOI-712 b, possesses a hydrogen-helium envelope fraction of approximately 10%, indicating that even at close-in orbits, these mini-Neptunes retain significant gaseous envelopes.

Doping TiO$_2$ with p-block elements like nitrogen and carbon is a promising strategy to tune its electronic and magnetic characteristics. This study employs hybrid DFT calculations to investigate the doping of rutile TiO$_2$ with nitrogen and carbon, analyzing the resulting electronic and magnetic properties. Our findings indicate that N-doping introduces a narrow band gap and induces a magnetic moment of 1 $\mu_B$ per unit cell, whereas C-doping yields a non-magnetic system with a reduced band gap. Furthermore, N-doping creates a new occupied band within the gap, which is primarily composed of N-2p states, while C-doping results in a gap narrowing driven by the formation of a C-2p/Ti-3d hybridized band. Finally, we determined that N-doping stabilizes the rutile phase, whereas C-doping favors the anatase structure.

We introduce the concept of "elastic potential," a metric designed to evaluate the efficacy of new physics searches by quantifying the reduction in background events resulting from specific signal selection criteria. Utilizing this metric, we scrutinize background suppression strategies for the $t\bar{t}$ + photon production channel at the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC). We demonstrate that the inclusion of photon isolation requirements is essential for suppressing the dominant QCD background, whereas the application of transverse momentum ($p_T$) thresholds on the photon is found to be largely ineffective.

The study of the Ramsey upper density of infinite graphs, denoted as $\overline{d}^*(G)$, examines the smallest value $d \in [0,1]$ such that any complete graph with sufficiently large vertex set and edge coloring using two colors contains a copy of $G$ within at least one color class having edge density no less than $d$. This paper establishes that for every integer $k \geq 3$, the $\overline{d}^*(G)$ value for the family of all $n$-vertex graphs containing an infinite factor of cycles of length $k$ is exactly $1/2$. Furthermore, it is shown that for any integer $k \geq 3$, the $\overline{d}^*(G)$ value for the family of graphs with at least one cycle of length $k$ is $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2k}$.

This study examines the simulation of scalar quantum electrodynamics (sQED) through quantum information techniques, with a specific focus on the impact of noise and the use of qudits. We evaluate two distinct simulation approaches: one utilizing noisy qubits and another employing noisy qutrits to represent the scalar field. Our analysis reveals that simulating with noisy qutrits offers a significant advantage, reducing the noise level in physical observables by a factor of approximately 100 compared to noisy qubit simulations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that representing the scalar field with noisy qutrits allows for the accurate reproduction of key features, including the narrow and wide resonance peaks observed in the vacuum's response to an external charge.

We present a comprehensive study of dense positron plasma formation within the Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) regime, utilizing Monte Carlo simulations of laser-target interactions. Our work details the generation of polarized positrons and the resulting dense, polarized positron plasma, with a specific focus on the impact of electron screening on the conversion of polarized photons into positron pairs. We demonstrate that this plasma exhibits a net polarization and possesses a high positron density, reaching approximately $10^{29} \text{ cm}^{-3}$ under specific laser conditions. Furthermore, we analyze the collective dynamics of this system, highlighting the generation of intense, linearly polarized positron beams.

This paper investigates finite groups $G$ where the diameter of the generating graph $\Gamma(G)$, denoted as $\text{diam}(\Gamma(G))$, remains bounded by a polynomial function of $|G|^{1/d}$ for some fixed $d$. The authors establish that if $G$ is an abelian group, it must be isomorphic to the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_p$ for a prime $p$. Furthermore, the study examines the case where $G$ is a $p$-group, demonstrating that if $G$ possesses an elementary abelian quotient of rank at least 3, then $\text{diam}(\Gamma(G))$ is infinite. Finally, the work explores groups $G$ with a non-trivial Fitting subgroup, proving that if $G$ is not isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_p$, the diameter is infinite.

This paper introduces the concept of geometric structures on differentiable stacks and Lie groupoids, demonstrating that such structures on stacks correspond precisely to specific equivariant structures defined on the associated Lie groupoids. Furthermore, it establishes a one-to-one relationship between geometric structures on a Lie groupoid $G$ and certain $G$-invariant geometric structures on the source manifold $X$ of $G$, where the invariance is taken with respect to the groupoid action.

The Dragon Infrared Dark Cloud (IRDC) is a dense region located within the Galactic plane, known for hosting a cluster of young massive stars. This formation process is hypothesized to occur through the gravitational collapse of dense filaments, which draw material from the surrounding cloud to form new stars. This study investigates the mass accumulation of these stars by analyzing 1.1 mm continuum data obtained from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA). The analysis reveals a cluster of approximately 100 young stellar objects (YSOs) situated within a 0.4 pc wide region. These YSOs are organized into two distinct groups: a northern population of ~60 members, identified as protostars embedded in circumstellar disks, and a southern population of ~40 members, classified as Class 0 or I protostars lacking detectable disks. The spatial distribution of the northern group aligns with a prominent filamentary structure, whereas the southern group appears concentrated within a compact, roughly 0.1 pc core. The presence of a massive core surrounded by numerous forming stars suggests that the cluster's central region has already reached its final stellar population. This work establishes the existence of one-step recurrences for any reasonably mixing stationary random field on the sphere, specifically demonstrating that the field's values at a point can be approximated by those at a point displaced by a single geodesic distance. This result serves as the spherical counterpart to classical findings by Dynkin and others regarding stationary fields on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with translation-invariant structures. Furthermore, the paper investigates the specific case of the sphere $S^2$, offering a novel proof for the well-known Yaglom theorem that characterizes the Wigner–Szeg\H{o} limit spectrum of the spherical harmonic coefficients for the fully mixed spherical case.

The rheological characteristics of liquid foams are significantly influenced by surface roughness, a factor that has been largely overlooked in previous research. This study investigates the frictional behavior of dry liquid foams flowing over rough surfaces, utilizing both experimental methods and theoretical modeling. Experiments were conducted on a Hele-Shaw cell with a rough bottom plate, employing a roughness element size ($\delta$) ranging from 0.01 to 0.1 times the foam bubble diameter ($d$). Results indicate that the frictional stress ($\sigma_f$) exhibits a non-monotonic relationship with surface roughness, peaking at an intermediate roughness level. This maximum friction occurs when the roughness scale is comparable to the bubble diameter ($\delta \approx d$). The observed behavior is explained by a theoretical framework based on the interplay between the foam's yield stress and the capillary pressure generated by surface tension. Specifically, friction reaches its highest point when the roughness scale allows the yield stress to be maximized while simultaneously minimizing the capillary pressure required for bubbles to traverse the roughness elements.

Skin cancer is a critical health issue that requires early diagnosis and treatment to prevent metastasis. While deep learning has proven effective for skin cancer detection, it often struggles with imbalanced datasets, where minority classes are underrepresented. This study introduces a novel approach to identify and address such imbalances by detecting outliers using entropy. We evaluated the method on the widely used ISIC 2018 dataset, which contains images of melanoma and other skin lesions. The results indicate that the proposed outlier detection technique successfully identifies imbalances in the data. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that correcting these imbalances significantly enhances the performance of deep learning models.

We examine the elastic fingering of a fluid driven through a rotating Hele-Shaw cell by a pressure gradient. This system is modeled using a two-dimensional approach that incorporates Coriolis forces and assumes the cell's rotation axis is perpendicular to the cell plane. The analysis reveals that rotation significantly alters the instability, causing the primary finger to split into multiple branches. Furthermore, the study identifies a critical rotation rate beyond which the flow becomes unstable to transverse perturbations, leading to chaotic motion.

The detection of two distinct isomers of ethynyl cyclopentadiene within the TMC-1 molecular cloud, specifically 1-ethynyl cyclopentadiene and 2-ethynyl cyclopentadiene, has been confirmed through the identification of 11 and 10 new rotational transitions, respectively, utilizing the IRAM 30-m and NOEMA arrays. These findings were supported by the construction of comprehensive rotational spectra for both molecules using the Leiden Atomic and Molecular Database (LAMDA) and the program COLG, which were subsequently employed to identify the spectral lines in observational data. The derived abundances for these isomers, relative to H$_2$CO, are $(1.1 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-10}$ and $(1.0 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-10}$, while their rotational constants were determined with high precision. Notably, the observed abundance ratio of the two isomers is approximately 1, indicating a lack of significant preference for either form. Furthermore, the detection of the CN analogue of cyclopentadiene (CN-cyclopentadiene) via the identification of 11 new transitions yields an abundance of $(1.0 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-10}$ relative to H$_2$CO.
